title: London session of the USD bond market recommended closed all day for the Boxing Day substitute — on a day London is statutorily shut anyway, with New York trading a full session
source: NEWS: sifma.org/resources/guides-playbooks/holiday-schedule ('Holiday Schedule'), fetched direct 2026-09-05 (HTTP 200, 298,926 bytes) and parsed card-by-card (h3 name / date / note) with region attribution fixed to the page's own 'U.S. / U.K. / Japan Holiday Recommendations' <h2> headings, then re-parsed independently out of the page's embedded Next.js flight payload (121 cards across all six panels) by this session. The U.K. 2026 panel's 17th card reads exactly ['Boxing Day (Substitute)', 'Monday, December 28, 2026'] with NO early-close note attached — the full-closure shape, distinct from the 'Early Close' entries elsewhere on the same page. The causing holiday is independently statutory: gov.uk/bank-holidays.json (HTTP 200, 22,207 bytes, the England-and-Wales division) lists '2026-12-28 | Boxing Day | Substitute day', 2026-12-26 falling on a Saturday. Cross-checked the same day against the page's U.S. panel, which carries NO 2026-12-28 card at all — its December entries are the 12-24 early close, the 12-25 closure and the 12-31 early close — so the recommended US fixed-income tape runs a full session while London is dark. Filed estimate on three counts, identical to the four sifma-* entries already on this calendar: the confirmed-prefix taxonomy in market-events-data.ts has no slot for an industry trade association's recommended schedule, this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep, and SIFMA's own page states its schedule is a recommendation ('On behalf of financial markets participants, SIFMA recommends a holiday schedule for financial markets in the U.S., U.K. and Japan') rather than a market-wide halt each firm is bound by.
notes: DISCOVERED during the sifma-japan-early-close-2026-12-28 initial research (2026-09-05); RESEARCHED and AMENDED by its own lane 2026-09-05 (docs/research/events/sifma-uk-bond-market-closure-2026-12-28.md), which re-fetched every primary rather than inheriting them. TITLE AMENDED in that PR: this is the LONDON SESSION OF THE US DOLLAR BOND MARKET, not the gilt market. SIFMA's page states its scope verbatim — 'All SIFMA holiday recommendations apply to the trading of U.S. dollar-denominated government securities, mortgage- and asset-backed securities, over-the-counter investment-grade and high-yield corporate bonds, municipal bonds and secondary money market trading in bankers' acceptances, commercial paper and Yankee and Euro certificates of deposit' — so the three regional panels are three TIME ZONES of one US-dollar market, not three asset classes, and GILTS ARE OUT OF SCOPE. WHY IT EARNS A ROW: it is the CAUSE of the Japan-panel entry already tracked on this date (sifma-japan-early-close-2026-12-28). On 2026-12-28 that one dollar market sits in three states at once: London recommended fully closed (this entry), Tokyo recommended closed early at 15:00 JST, New York running a normal session — the exact INVERSE of the triple three days later on 2026-12-31 (sifma-bond-early-close-2026-12-31, jpx-market-closure-2026-12-31). This is the FIRST U.K.-panel entry on this calendar. KEY FINDING, and it is what distinguishes this card from its US-panel siblings: IT IS REDUNDANT WITH STATUTE. 2026-12-28 is a gov.uk England-and-Wales bank holiday, so London equities and gilts are dark whatever SIFMA recommends — measured, ^FTSE printed NO BAR on 37 of 37 gov.uk weekday bank holidays that were New York sessions since 2019 (detector = a weekday with a ^GSPC bar and no ^FTSE bar; 37/38 precision, the one false positive being the 2020-12-22 Yahoo data gap; 37/37 recall). That is the opposite of sifma-bond-market-closure-2026-11-11 and -2026-10-12, where NYSE trades a full session and the SIFMA card IS the information. Here the card is the Japan entry's cause, not news of its own. STRUCTURE: the U.K. panel is the strictest of the three — 36 of 36 cards across 2026 and 2027 are full closures with ZERO 'Early Close' strings, where the U.S. 2026 panel carries eight and the Japan 2026 panel two, so Good Friday 2026-04-03 is a 12:00 ET half day in New York and a full closure in London. And 9 of the 18 U.K. 2026 cards are US-only holidays (MLK, Presidents, Memorial, Juneteenth, US Independence observed, Labor, Columbus, Veterans, Thanksgiving) against 9 gov.uk statutory ones; 2026-05-25 is rendered as two cards, Memorial Day and Spring Bank Holiday, for one date. IMPACT LOW, and measured rather than assumed — a TRIPLE NULL, all three attributions failing a control: ^GSPC on 170 London-shut/New-York-open sessions since 1990 runs 0.702% mean |close-to-close| against 0.745% month-matched (Welch t = -0.64); EWU's volume gap to SPY (+0.162 raw) does not clear a month-and-weekday-matched control (+0.118, permutation p = 0.096, n = 140 vs 971); EWU's volatility compression (0.864x move ratio, t = -2.85 unpaired) is NOT attributable to its dark underlying (paired against EWJ, whose Tokyo underlying is open, -0.086 with 74/142 negative, p = 0.337, while FXB — whose FX market never closes at all — compresses MOST at 0.802x); and EWU adds nothing over SPY about where the FTSE reopens (b = 0.064, t = 0.48, R-squared 0.131 -> 0.133, with SPY's sign agreement of 58.7% beating EWU's 55.9%). The 11-11 sibling's half-depth execution guard therefore DOES NOT TRANSFER to this date and the ledger explicitly declines to import it. No house playbook is calendar-, holiday- or rates-keyed (docs/plans/trade-playbooks.md and docs/research/multi-symbol-sweep.md grepped 2026-09-05 for 'holiday|gilt|london|boxing|sifma|closure|ewu|ftse|year-end': zero hits in both), and this repo tracks no UK-listed symbol. HONEST LIMITS: SIFMA's 2027 U.K. panel reads 'Christmas Day / Friday, December 24, 2027' and 'Boxing Day / None' while gov.uk dates statutory substitutes on 2027-12-27 and 2027-12-28, and it lists Juneteenth on a Saturday and July 4 on a Sunday unshifted where the U.S. panel shifts both — so it is either genuinely year-by-year or loosely maintained; this entry is filed on the 2026 panel alone, and no U.K. card in either year carries a tentative flag where every 2027 Japan card does. It is a recommendation to member firms, NOT an exchange closure. The London Stock Exchange's own calendar was FETCHED this session and is NOT MACHINE-READABLE (londonstockexchange.com/equity-trading/business-days, HTTP 200, 54,995 bytes, a client-rendered Angular shell whose body strips to five text cells with no dates), which is why the equity-hours claim above is empirical rather than sourced from the exchange.
